name: mr-studio-multisession
description: A coding agent has worked across many sessions on the MR Studio web app and accumulated durable memories. Each task is a fresh session: the agent is about to do something and needs the relevant prior memories pulled into context. `relevant_ids` is the human-labeled gold set of memories that actually matter for that task.
query_note: Each task carries two phrasings of the same request. `query` is written the way a developer who knows the codebase would type it, and shares vocabulary with the gold memories. `paraphrase` describes the same task from the outside — a bug report or a product ask — deliberately avoiding the words used in the memories. The gap between the two is the honest measure of how much the default lexical retriever depends on shared wording.
distractor_note: `distractors` are additional plausible memories from the same project that are not relevant to any task. They exist to grow the store for the scaling experiment, which tests whether recall cost stays flat as memory accumulates.

memories.text: The MR Studio web app is a React + Vite frontend with an Express backend, written in TypeScript. Run the dev server with `npm run dev` from the project root; it listens on port 5002.
The database is PostgreSQL accessed through the Drizzle ORM. The schema lives in shared/schema.ts and migrations are managed with drizzle-kit.
Bookings are stored in UTC in the database and converted to the Asia/Tbilisi timezone only in the UI layer. Never persist local time.
The customer chatbot uses Google Gemini (gemini-2.0-flash-exp). Its system prompt and the list of services and prices live in server/gemini-chat.ts.
Known bug: the booking confirmation email sometimes sends twice because the email handler is not idempotent. Dedupe by tracking sent emails per booking id before retrying.
Authentication uses signed session cookies via express-session. Admin routes are guarded by the requireAdmin middleware in server/auth.ts.
Uploaded images go to object storage; the ACL logic is in server/objectAcl.ts. Public read is allowed only for files under the gallery/ prefix; everything else stays private.
Gemini occasionally returns an empty response. server/gemini-chat.ts must fall back to a default message instead of throwing, otherwise the chat widget crashes.
Frontend styling uses Tailwind with custom CSS tokens defined in client/src/index.css. Do not hardcode hex colors inside components.
Currently implementing multilingual support for the chatbot (Georgian 'ka' and English 'en'); the language is passed from the client and selects which system prompt is used.
Next step: add rate limiting to the public chat endpoint /api/chat to prevent abuse of the Gemini API key. No limiter exists yet.
Replaced the old hardcoded services list on the landing page with data fetched from the /api/services endpoint.
Email notifications are sent through the helper in server/email-notifications.ts using the studio's SMTP credentials from environment variables.
Calendar sync writes confirmed bookings to Google Calendar via server/google-calendar.ts using a service account; a sync failure must not block the booking from being saved.

tasks.query: Fix the bug where customers receive two confirmation emails for a single booking.
tasks.paraphrase: Customers complain they get duplicate messages in their inbox after reserving a slot.

tasks.query: Add rate limiting to the chat endpoint so the Gemini API key cannot be abused.
tasks.paraphrase: Stop people from hammering the assistant endpoint and running up our LLM bill.

tasks.query: A booking shows the wrong time to the customer. Investigate how timezones are handled for bookings.
tasks.paraphrase: A client saw the wrong hour for their appointment. Check how clock offsets are handled.

tasks.query: Update the list of services and prices the chatbot tells customers about.
tasks.paraphrase: Change what the assistant quotes for treatments and their cost.

tasks.query: Make the gallery images publicly viewable while keeping all other uploads private.
tasks.paraphrase: Let visitors see the photo showcase while other uploads stay locked down.

tasks.query: Add a new admin-only settings page and make sure it is protected like the other admin routes.
tasks.paraphrase: Build a settings screen only staff can open, protected like the rest of the back office.

tasks.query: The chat widget sometimes crashes when Gemini replies. Make the chat resilient to bad responses.
tasks.paraphrase: The assistant window dies when the model returns nothing. Harden it.

distractors.text: CI runs on GitHub Actions from .github/workflows/ci.yml on every pull request and on pushes to main.
Production deploys are manual: build the frontend, then restart the Node process behind the reverse proxy.
Static marketing pages are pre-rendered at build time and served from the CDN edge cache.
We use Vitest for unit tests and Playwright for the two end-to-end smoke flows.
Bumped the Vite version to 5.4 and removed the legacy rollup workaround from the config.
The Playwright smoke test is flaky on cold starts because the dev server needs about four seconds to boot.
Analytics events are sent to a self-hosted Plausible instance; no third-party trackers are used anywhere.
The favicon and social preview images are generated from a single source SVG at build time.
Removed 14 unused npm dependencies and cut the production bundle by roughly 180 kilobytes.
Error monitoring uses a self-hosted Sentry; the DSN is read from the SENTRY_DSN environment variable.
Log output is structured JSON in production and human-readable pretty print in development.
Safari 16 renders the sticky footer one pixel off; the workaround uses translateZ(0) on the container.
Migrated the contact form markup to semantic fieldset and legend elements for screen readers.
The repository uses pnpm workspaces with the client, server and shared packages in separate folders.
Commit messages follow Conventional Commits so the changelog can be generated automatically.
Added a robots.txt and an XML sitemap generated from the public route manifest.
The staging database occasionally holds a stale materialized view; refreshing it manually resolves the drift.
Feature flags are plain environment variables read once at server startup, not a third-party service.
Dates in the admin tables are displayed in ISO format to avoid ambiguity for staff in different locales.
Replaced the custom scroll spy on the landing page with an IntersectionObserver.
The design tokens were exported from Figma and checked in as JSON under design/tokens.json.
Long-running report generation happens in a background worker, not inside a request handler.
Hot module replacement drops the websocket connection when the laptop wakes from sleep; a page refresh fixes it.
Split the giant utils module into four focused modules and removed the circular import.
Fonts are self-hosted as woff2 subsets; nothing is loaded from Google Fonts at runtime.
Form validation logic is shared between client and server through the schemas in the shared package.
Added skeleton loading states to the three slowest pages in the admin dashboard.
The pagination component computes the wrong page count when the result set is exactly one page long.
Backups run nightly with pg_dump to encrypted object storage and are retained for thirty days.
Secrets never enter the repository; local development reads them from an untracked .env file.
Converted the remaining class components in the admin area to function components with hooks.
The health check endpoint at /healthz returns build metadata and the database connectivity status.
Database migrations run as a separate deploy step so a failed migration never leaves a half-started server.
Very large uploads time out behind the proxy because the default body size limit was never raised.
Documented the local setup steps in CONTRIBUTING so new contributors can start without asking.
Lint and format are enforced by ESLint and Prettier through a pre-commit hook.
The API returns problem+json error bodies so the client can render messages without string matching.
Added an npm script that seeds the local database with a small realistic fixture set.
Two integration tests share a fixture and fail when run in parallel; they are pinned to one worker for now.
Client-side routing uses wouter rather than react-router to keep the bundle small.
